item 37 one host finalizer / one exit write site
purpose: Define one total host-owned process-exit contract for every CommandEnvelope kind and for long-lived protocol servers.

correctsCandidateFormula.to: exitCode = map(HostTermination); admitted analysis derives HostTermination from lifecycle, required Coverage, verdict, durability, interruption, and required postconditions.

exitClasses.meaning: The requested operation completed; an analysis passed or was advisory; or a serve process completed cooperative shutdown.
A valid, sufficiently covered analysis completed and project-owned policy failed.
Usage, configuration, admission, compatibility, lookup-address, resolver failure, or mutation-precondition rejection.
The host produced an honest terminal result but required evidence, convergence, or negotiable recipe support was unavailable.
Host, provider, protocol, integrity, durability, required-delivery, contention, or output-materialization failure prevented reliable completion.
The user interrupted a finite (non-serve-stop) operation and cooperative cleanup ran where possible.

rules: A valid empty query result is success; absence is data unless the command addresses one required identity or uses a single-identity resolver.

Bad arguments, authored-config errors, unsupported schema majors, incompatible contributions, missing addressed identities, failed resolvers (including latest on empty domain), authority conflicts (ephemeral Plan when authoritative required), and failed mutation preconditions are request-rejected.
A query with an explicit completeness requirement that cannot be met is indeterminate.
Baseline compare against an unsupported/unnegotiable fingerprint recipe is indeterminate (never policy-failed via mass false net-new).

Host, datastore, provider-protocol, installation-I/O, ledger busy-timeout, required-delivery, and output-serialization failures are operational-failed; errorCodes distinguish retryable contention from corruption.
A mutation with a linked verification Run propagates that Run's success, policy-failed, indeterminate, or operational-failed termination while retaining the mutation receipt.

A protocol server that shuts down normally OR completes cooperative SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup is success; a host/protocol fault is operational-failed; user-interrupt class is not used for clean serve stop.

invariants: Only the host finalizer constructs HostTermination; producers return domain results, Coverage reasons, observations, or typed faults and never numeric exits.
There is one normal process-boundary map from HostTermination.class to a numeric code and one controllable process-exit write site.
For finite CLI commands, CommandEnvelope.termination.class and .exitCode equal the process termination when serialization succeeds.
FailureResult is constructible without project identity or Run identity.
A policy verdict never becomes an Error, and an operational failure never becomes a Finding.
Optional Cloud/export failure cannot alter the local Run verdict; it changes process termination only when delivery was an explicit required postcondition.
A durability failure cannot report success for an authoritative Run even when analysis verdict is pass.
Signal handlers request cancellation; they do not contain an independent business-level exit mapper.
SIGKILL and runtime failures that prevent all finalization are outside the controllable exit contract.
Interruption or crash during authoritative publication must leave the ledger recoverable; recovery marks orphans abandoned, never sealed success (exit may still be interrupted).
Envelope projections keep analysis verdict and HostTermination visibly distinct fields.
Exit 0 is never by itself a durable attestation; callers requiring authority declare it as a required postcondition.
